analysis.title: Global Weekly Kickstart: Earnings are strong but acceleration is fading
key_insights: With 60% of the S&P 500 reported, Q3 EPS growth is tracking at 33% yoy, putting Q3 on track to match Q2 as one of the strongest quarters in recent decades outside recoveries.
Europe Q3 EPS growth is expected at 23%, ahead of expectations.
Energy and AI account for much of the headline growth. Median-company EPS growth is 12% in the US and 11% in Europe, which GS reads as healthy underlying breadth.
Growth is no longer accelerating and upgrades versus downgrades have moderated, pointing to softer momentum into 2027.
Market reactions to earnings are asymmetric: misses underperform by roughly twice as much as beats outperform.
Global equities were flat last week. Value outperformed Growth as an unwind in crowded AI positions weighed on Communication Services (-6.7%) and Technology (-1.4%).
The Nasdaq is down 9% since early October, while the S&P 500 ex-AI is up 8%.
GS commodities analysts raised their 2027 average Brent forecast to $88/bbl on elevated supply risks.
GS forecasts the US 10Y yield falling from 4.9% to 4.4% in 12 months, and Brent from $117.6 to $80/bbl.
GS forecasts gold at $5232/oz in 12 months (+34.3% from $3896).
Consensus 2026 EPS growth estimates: S&P 500 32.5%, STOXX 600 21.1%, MSCI AC World 35.4%. IT is 89.0% and Energy 95.6%.
Consensus 2027 EPS growth: S&P 500 16.4%, STOXX 600 8.6%, MSCI AC World 16.9%. Energy is -10.5% and Communication Services -5.8%.
The GS Bull/Bear Market Indicator is at 66%, with Shiller PE at 39.6 (97th percentile).
Valuation: US 12m fwd P/E is 18.4, US ex Big Tech 17.7, Europe 13.8, EM 8.7.
GS sector stance: US overweight Materials and Health Care. Europe overweight Financials, IT and Communication Services. Japan overweight Industrials, Financials, IT and Communication Services.
Week ahead: US mid-term elections and the employment report, Fed speakers, and Riksbank, Norges Bank and BoE rate decisions.
